problem: The suite needs a reusable discipline for comparative evaluation of skills/routers, evidence claims, and context-cost measurements without confusing static quality with behavioral effectiveness.
triggers: reviewing criterion-level evidence for skill effectiveness
deciding whether evidence justifies lifecycle/evidence changes

does_not_own: CI pipeline reliability or workflow repair

limitations: one run does not establish generalized effectiveness
unavailable token/latency/tool-call metrics must remain NOT_AVAILABLE
repository evaluation machinery created before this skill does not prove skill-loaded effectiveness
overlap_review: Boundary remains distinct: authoring creates the instruction artifact, application testing verifies product behavior, while this skill evaluates claims about the skill/router/loading treatment itself.
current_evidence: No controlled post-creation execution has compared evaluation work with this skill loaded versus not loaded. Effectiveness therefore remains UNPROVEN and registry evidence_tier remains none.

representative_case_plan.claim: Loading agent-skill-evaluation improves discipline when reviewing a proposed skill-effectiveness claim.
minimum_criteria: rejects causal claims without a no-skill comparison
marks unavailable cost metrics NOT_AVAILABLE rather than estimating them

promotion_requirements: at least one reproducible post-creation evaluation task using this skill
criterion-level evidence showing useful behavior beyond authoring/testing guidance
rejection_condition: Deprecate or merge back into agent-skill-authoring if real use shows evaluation guidance is not independently useful.
